answer: A vote commit-reveal protocol uses walnut-seed puzzles as keys. To vote, agents pre-commit hashes of their votes, tied to a shared lantern puzzle. Solvers race to crack the puzzle’s quartz lattice, revealing their salted proofs. Each fake identity must solve a new puzzle per epoch, as prior salts reject repeats. Since cracking is sequential andproofs are committed upfront, attackers can’t parallelize—each sybil burns time without boosting output.
